truths.truth: A provider response is bounded by BYTES inside the one concatenation point, and crossing it destroys the request instead of resolving with the full body
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/review-provider.mjs:276 MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES=4194304, :588-604 per-chunk count at the single `data += c` site with req.destroy(err) tagged OVER_RESPONSE, :639-640 failRequest maps the tag to reason 'over-response'. `node --test cadence-core/bin/review-provider.test.mjs` 69 pass / 0 fail; the ceiling test asserts reason 'over-response', code 1 and chunksEmitted === 5 of 8 (the stream was CUT), and the sibling test proves consult and detect-models are bounded by the same read path. Traced end to end: the 8x1MiB fake wire enters through runFaked and lands as the CLI envelope plus one provider event with outcome 'over-response', degraded true.

truths.truth: The HTTP failure envelope carries ONE shape - a capped, sanitized string excerpt - not the whole body
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/review-provider.mjs:676-693 bodyExcerpt (always String, cap MAX_HTTP_BODY_BYTES=1024 minus the truncation marker, sanitized through redactUrl + redactCredentials); the only two http fail sites, :1035 and :1131, both pass through it. Test 'RVP-01: the response is bounded by bytes Cadence owns, and the failure envelope is capped' (review-provider.test.mjs:1590) injects a 502 body echoing Bearer/key=/api_token/secret and asserts typeof string, <=1024 bytes, none of the planted substrings, and that the model diagnostic text survives. Green.

Each matches its test's own WATCHED FAILING AT header and quoted unpatched output: review-provider.test.mjs:1566 (e1e6c0a, observed reason 'internal' with a TypeError), :1630 (15b5d4c, observed ok:true carrying a line:0 finding), prose-agreement.test.mjs:573 (cdf8676, observed label 'timeout or no report'). truths.truth: The goal's 'sanitized excerpt' clause holds on provider-controlled input - a credential in the body cannot reach the failure envelope
truths.evidence: Reproduced, not merely read: replaying bodyExcerpt's exact logic (cadence-core/bin/review-provider.mjs:676-693) against the real lib/redact-url.mjs with a >4096-byte body whose sanitized window lands just over `room` returns an envelope ending `... \"password\":\"SUPERSECRET ...[truncated]` - the key name and 11 bytes of the value. Mechanism is the ordering at :683-686: the trailing-token safeguard runs only when `clean <= room`, so a window-edge-truncated credential whose quoted value lost its closing quote (CRED_VALUE's alternatives all fail) survives redaction and stays inside the first `room` bytes when the shrink lands just past the cap. SUMMARY.md:118-125 declares this as an open item with the mechanism confirmed, so it is disclosed, not hidden - but it is a hole in the goal clause, not merely beside it.

gaps.name: bodyExcerpt leaks a credential fragment at the sanitize-window edge
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the goal's 'sanitized excerpt' clause does not hold for one reachable class of provider-controlled body, even though AC2's own fixture passes
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/review-provider.mjs:683-686 - the trailing-token safeguard is gated on `Buffer.byteLength(clean) <= room`, so when redaction shrinks the 4096-byte window to just PAST the cap the window-edge-truncated credential survives inside the first `room` bytes. Reproduced against the real cadence-core/bin/lib/redact-url.mjs: the returned excerpt ends `\"password\":\"SUPERSECRET ...[truncated]` (key name plus 11 bytes of value). Cause is that a quoted value cut before its closing quote matches none of CRED_VALUE's three alternatives (lib/redact-url.mjs:122), so redactCredentials leaves it whole. Declared at SUMMARY.md:118-125; the related quadratic in redactUrl that forces the window at all is SUMMARY.md:126-130.
gaps.missing: A bounded notion of edge-adjacent tail: drop the trailing partial token whenever the source was windowed, regardless of whether `clean` fits, without gutting an ordinary long diagnostic (the RVP-01 fixture's 4096-byte no-whitespace padding is the case both attempted repairs broke). Fixing the redactUrl quadratic instead removes the window and the hole together. A test fixture in the shape above (window shrinks to just over `room`, credential at the window edge) belongs beside the existing envelope tests.
